title: Microsoft Teams: latest meeting experience for anonymous join on Safari and Firefox web
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, anonymous-join controls and licensing statements are supported by the record and Microsoft Learn. Searches found no documentation specifying the refresh's default state, a separate experience-selection setting or refresh-specific licensing terms.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Anonymous participants are people whose identities Teams has not verified.
claims.quote: In meetings and events hosted by your organization, anonymous users are users whose identities aren't verified.

claims.claim: People not signed in to Teams with a work or school account can be anonymous participants.
claims.quote:
These users can include:
- Users who aren't signed in to Teams with a work or school account.

claims.claim: Teams displays Unverified next to the name of an anonymous user joining unverified.
claims.quote: When anonymous users join a meeting unverified, Unverified appears next to their name.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The organisation-wide anonymous-join setting governs anonymous meeting access across the tenant.
claims.quote: You can control whether anonymous users can join meetings for your entire organization or for specific organizers and groups.

claims.claim: Per-organiser meeting policies control which users or groups can host meetings allowing anonymous participants.
claims.quote: To control which users or groups can host meetings that allow anonymous participants, assign a per-organizer meeting policy to each organizer or group.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Lobby policies affect how anonymous participants join meetings.
claims.quote: When anonymous meeting join is turned on, lobby policies affect how anonymous participants join meetings.

claims.claim: Organiser meeting options also govern anonymous meeting access.
claims.quote:
Your organizers have the following setting in their Meeting options to manage anonymous meeting join for their meetings:
- Require unverified participants to verify their info before joining

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn lists Edge, Chrome, Firefox and Safari as browsers on which Teams for Web is available.
claims.quote: Teams on the Teams for Web client is available on Microsoft Edge, Chrome, Firefox, and Safari browsers.

claims.claim: The tenant anonymous-join control is in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting settings > Participants > Anonymous users can join a meeting.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings.
Under Participants, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -DisableAnonymousJoin $true sets the tenant control to block anonymous join.
claims.quote:
Determines whether anonymous users are blocked from joining meetings in the tenant. Set this to TRUE to block anonymous users from joining. Set this to FALSE to allow anonymous users to join meetings.
-Identity
The only valid input is Global

claims.claim: The organiser control is in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified toggle Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false prevents anonymous join for organisers with that policy.
claims.quote:
To prevent anonymous participants from joining meetings organized by users or groups with this policy, use this script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn says the organisation-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting is going away.
claims.quote: The Anonymous users can join a meeting organization-wide setting is going away.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends leaving the organisation-wide setting On and using the per-organiser unverified anonymous-join policy instead.
claims.quote: We recommend leaving this setting On and using the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified per-organizer meeting policy to manage anonymous meeting join instead.

claims.claim: Meeting policy changes might take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes to meeting policies might take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Email-code verified anonymous join is governed separately from unverified anonymous join and is not the experience refresh.
claims.quote: If you turn off the organization-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting and Anonymous users can join a meeting after verifying is set to No, anonymous users can't join meetings in your organization.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn setting selecting this Safari and Firefox anonymous meeting experience was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Safari Firefox anonymous meeting refresh admin policy default rollout 329253; "Teams" "Safari" "Firefox" "anonymous" "meeting experience". Read anonymous-access, Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration and Teams for Web; no experience-selection control found.

claims.claim: Teams for Web documentation does not identify browser-version requirements specific to this anonymous-join refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Safari Firefox anonymous join performance improvements meeting experience license price browser versions. Read Teams for Web and browser-support search excerpts; Firefox's latest three and Safari's latest two versions are general requirements, not refresh-specific.
